routes.notes: Individual response to 1,4-butanediol varies considerably owing to differences in alcohol dehydrogenase enzyme activity. Because effects take longer to manifest than with GHB, premature redosing before the initial dose has taken effect is a frequent contributor to overdose. Recommendations mention starting at 1 mL for new users. Food greatly increases onset time.

records.summary: 1,4-Butanediol is a synthetic diol compound first synthesized in 1890 by Dutch chemist Pieter Johannes Dekkers. It is considered habit-forming[cite:skryabin-2023-review] and carries additional health risks compared to GHB, notably liver toxicity.

records.summary: 1P-ETH-LAD is a semisynthetic psychedelic of the lysergamide class and a suspected prodrug of ETH-LAD[citation-needed], structurally related to both LSD and 1P-LSD. Developed as a designer drug, it is reported to be moderately to significantly more potent than LSD. It remains largely unresearched[citation-needed] and is classified as a research chemical.

Its effects have been compared to those of benzylpiperazine and methamphetamine, though very little is known about its recreational use profile.

Due to the near-total absence of research or documented human use, it should be approached with extreme caution.

records.summary: 25B-NBOH is a synthetic psychedelic of the substituted phenethylamine class, derived from 2C-B through N-benzylation.[citation-needed] First synthesized in 2011 by Martin Hansen at the University of Copenhagen, it is a close structural analog of 25B-NBOMe and is reported to share most of its properties, with moderately reduced potency and a shorter duration. It produces visually dominant and stimulating psychedelic effects, acting as a potent serotonin receptor agonist at 5-HT2A and 5-HT2C receptors.[citation-needed]

routes.notes: The blotter should be held under the tongue for 15 to 30 minutes to allow adequate absorption, as this compound has very low bioavailability when swallowed. Deaths have been reported at heavy doses.

Insufflation of 25B-NBOMe presents substantially increased overdose risk compared to other routes, as nasal absorption occurs rapidly and accurate dose measurement is extremely difficult. This route has been implicated in multiple deaths. Use by this method is strongly discouraged.

This compound has very low bioavailability when swallowed, rendering oral ingestion largely ineffective. Sublingual absorption or insufflation produces significantly greater effects at equivalent doses.

It is an N-benzyl derivative of 2C-B, first described by Ralf Heim at the Free University of Berlin. The substance had virtually no history of human use before appearing on the research chemical market in 2010. Compared to its parent compound 2C-B, 25B-NBOMe is reported to be approximately sixteen times more potent.

records.summary: 25C-NBOH is a synthetic psychedelic of the substituted phenethylamine class, produced through N-benzylation of the psychedelic 2C-C.[citation-needed] First synthesized in 2011 by Martin Hansen at the University of Copenhagen, it has since appeared as a designer drug.[citation-needed] It is known for producing predominantly visual and stimulating psychedelic effects, with serotonin receptor affinity comparable to its structural relative 25C-NBOMe.
records.title: 25C-NBOH

tolerance.baseline_tolerance: Approximately 2 weeks in the absence of further consumption
tolerance.full_tolerance: Develops almost immediately after ingestion.

routes.notes: Nasal administration carries a substantially elevated risk of fatal overdose and is strongly discouraged. The compound's high potency combined with a narrow threshold between pharmacologically active and dangerous quantities makes precise microgram-level dosing impractical through this route. When handling the substance in pure powder form, appropriate laboratory precautions—including protective eyewear, gloves, and a respirator—are necessary to avoid unintended exposure via inhalation or mucous membrane contact.

For effective absorption, the substance must be held sublingually or against the buccal mucosa for 10–20 minutes; if swallowed immediately, bioavailability is substantially reduced. Users typically experience a pronounced metallic taste and localized numbness of the tongue and oral tissues, which may persist for up to one hour. The margin between an active dose and a potentially lethal dose is exceptionally narrow—fatalities have been reported at doses as low as 4 mg (4000 µg), and overdose may occur at approximately twice a common dose.

binding_sites.efficacy: Described as partial agonist in some sources, implied to be full agonist in others

records.summary: 25C-NBOMe is a synthetic psychedelic of the substituted phenethylamine class and a member of the 25x-NBOMe series, a group of potent compounds derived from the 2C-x family. Discovered in 2003 by Ralf Heim at the Free University of Berlin, it is derived from 2C-C through the addition of an N-benzyl methoxy group, resulting in roughly a sixteen-fold increase in potency. It first appeared on the research chemical market around 2010 and is active in the microgram range.

records.summary: 25D-NBOMe is a synthetic psychedelic of the substituted phenethylamine class[citation-needed], derived from 2C-D through the addition of an N-benzyl methoxy group[citation-needed]. It was discovered in 2003 by Ralf Heim at the Free University of Berlin and emerged as a recreational substance around 2010 through online research chemical vendors. It acts as a potent partial agonist at the 5-HT2A receptor, producing primarily visual and stimulating effects with roughly sixteen-fold greater potency than its parent compound.
records.title: 25D-NBOMe

tolerance.baseline_tolerance: Approximately 2-3 weeks for tolerance to fully reset after a single experience.
tolerance.full_tolerance: Develops immediately after use.

routes.notes: Produces a strong, unpleasant metallic chemical taste and a distinct numbness of the tongue and mouth that can persist for up to an hour. Associated with a significant body load manifesting as vasoconstriction. Most samples found are not consistently dosed and are observed to have hotspots. It is highly advised to start at a lower dosage.

records.summary: 25E-NBOH is a synthetic psychedelic of the substituted phenethylamine class, specifically an N-benzylated derivative of 2C-E.[citation-needed] It was first developed by Martin Hansen at the University of Copenhagen in 2010 for use as a brain imaging agent.[citation-needed] It has since appeared as a designer drug, first identified on seized blotter paper in Brazil in 2018.[citation-needed] 25E-NBOH is reported to share most properties with 25E-NBOMe but with moderately reduced potency and a shorter duration.
records.title: 25E-NBOH

tolerance.baseline_tolerance: 2-4 days to return to baseline tolerance in the absence of further consumption.
cross_tolerance: Serotonergic psychedelics (cross-tolerance is present but not uniform across all compounds; some psychedelics may be significantly affected while others experience only slight reduction in effects)
tolerance.full_tolerance: Tolerance to the effects of 25E-NBOH develops almost immediately following ingestion.
tolerance.half_tolerance: Approximately 1-2 days for tolerance to reduce to half of its peak level.

routes.notes: This substance is typically taken by holding blotter paper or liquid solution beneath the tongue for absorption through the oral mucosa. Compounds in the NBOMe class are known for significant variation in individual response, making it advisable to begin with doses at the lower end of reported ranges.

records.summary: 25E-NBOMe is a synthetic psychedelic of the substituted phenethylamine class, derived from 2C-E through N-benzylation. It is a potent 5-HT2A receptor agonist that produces effects similar to related compounds such as 25I-NBOMe and 25C-NBOMe. Typically distributed on blotters, it has been sold as a research chemical and is sometimes misrepresented as LSD. Notable risks include significant vasoconstriction and heavy body load, with high doses posing potentially life-threatening cardiovascular effects.

records.summary: 25I-NBMD is a synthetic psychedelic of the substituted phenethylamine class, specifically an N-benzylated derivative of 2C-I.[cite:halberstadt-2014-pmc3866097] It was discovered in 2006 by a research team led by David Nichols at Purdue University. Closely related to the 25X-NBOMe series, it is a highly potent compound that acts as a partial agonist at the 5-HT2A receptor.[citation-needed] As a research chemical, it has very limited documentation regarding its effects and safety profile in humans.

records.summary: 25I-NBOH is a synthetic psychedelic of the substituted phenethylamine class, specifically an N-benzylated derivative of 2C-I. First synthesized in 2006 by a team led by David Nichols at Purdue University, it is a close structural analog of 25I-NBOMe and is reported to share most of its properties, though with moderately reduced potency and a shorter duration. It is a known metabolite of 25I-NBOMe and has also been encountered as a designer drug.[cite:pmid-26378134]
records.title: 25I-NBOH

tolerance.full_tolerance: Tolerance to the effects of 25I-NBOH develops almost immediately after ingestion.
tolerance.half_tolerance: Approximately 1 week for tolerance to reduce to half in the absence of further consumption.

routes.notes: Sublingual administration is the most widely used method for this substance. Users commonly report a pronounced metallic taste and numbness in the mouth. Doses at the heavy end of the range have been linked to fatal outcomes and are highly discouraged.

Insufflation is strongly discouraged for this substance due to its rapid absorption through nasal membranes, the difficulty of accurately measuring active doses in the microgram range, and numerous documented fatalities associated with this route. Heavy dosages are discouraged to the highest degree.

records.summary: 25iP-NBOMe is a synthetic psychedelic of the substituted phenethylamine class, specifically an N-benzylated derivative of the hallucinogen 2C-iP. It has emerged as a rarely encountered novel designer drug[citation-needed] and remains largely unresearched. Reported to be extremely potent with stimulating qualities, it may produce uncomfortable body load and potentially dangerous vasoconstriction at higher doses. Very limited information is available regarding its safety profile and pharmacological properties.

routes.bioavailability_notes:
A very large portion of the drug is broken down by the liver before it reaches the bloodstream, resulting in relatively low bioavailability
The primary metabolite BDMPAA reaches concentrations roughly 280 times higher than the parent compound, reflecting extensive first-pass processing
routes.notes: 2C-B exhibits a notably steep dose-response relationship, particularly within the 12–24 mg range, where differences of just 2 mg can substantially alter both the intensity and qualitative nature of the experience. Careful, incremental dosing is recommended when establishing individual sensitivity.

Insufflation of 2C-B causes significant irritation to nasal mucosa, typically producing intense burning and pain. Due to the compound's caustic properties, this route is generally considered unpleasant and is often avoided in favor of oral administration.

Intravenous use presents significant hazards, including potential damage to veins and risk of localized infection at the injection site. Unpredictable chaotic onset compared to oral with severe localized pain. This route of administration is strongly discouraged.

routes.half_life_notes: Peak blood concentrations are typically reached approximately 2.3 hours after oral ingestion. At a 30 mg oral dose, mean peak plasma levels of 5.4 ng/mL have been observed, while a 20 mg dose produces mean peak levels of approximately 3.3 ng/mL.

records.summary: 2C-B is a synthetic psychedelic of the phenethylamine class and perhaps the most well-known member of the 2C-x family, which are structurally related to mescaline.[citation-needed] First synthesized by Alexander Shulgin in 1974[cite:poulie-2020-dark-classics-nbomes], he saw the possibility as an aid in psychiatric therapy.[cite:shulgin-carter-1975-centrally-active-phenethylamines] 2C-B is characterized by warm, colorful visuals, mild entactogenic qualities, and a prominent body component.[citation-needed][citation-needed] It is generally considered more manageable than classical psychedelics like LSD or psilocybin[citation-needed], though it is notably dose-sensitive.[citation-needed]
records.title: 2C-B

tolerance.baseline_tolerance: Tolerance appears to diminish relatively quickly, with effects returning to near-baseline levels after 5-7 days of abstinence.
cross_tolerance: Partial cross-tolerance with serotonergic psychedelics (asymmetric; other psychedelics may reduce 2C-B effects, but 2C-B typically does not diminish effects of subsequent psychedelic use)
tolerance.full_tolerance: Unlike most serotonergic psychedelics, 2C-B exhibits an unusual tolerance profile. Tolerance develops slowly even with repeated consecutive use, and the substance can often be redosed multiple times with minimal reduction in effect intensity. Some users report sustained multi-day use with only gradual tolerance accumulation.

routes.notes: Individual sensitivity to 2C-B-FLY varies considerably. Some individuals report pronounced effects at doses typically classified as light, whereas others may require amounts in the moderate-to-strong range to achieve similar intensity.

Dosage information for this route remains limited, with isolated reports suggesting doses in the range of approximately 8 mg. Insufflation produces a faster onset and shorter overall duration than oral use. This route is associated with pronounced nasal irritation and discomfort, and many users have abandoned it due to the caustic nature of the compound.

It has been primarily sold online as a designer drug in European markets.[citation-needed]

records.summary: 3-Me-PCPy is an arylcyclohexylamine derivative[cite:doi-10-1002-dta-1468] with an uncommon dual pharmacological profile, producing both dissociative and stimulant effects. Unlike most substances in its class, it combines potent NMDA antagonism with triple monoamine reuptake inhibition affecting serotonin, dopamine, and noradrenaline. It also displays high affinity for sigma receptors. This broad spectrum of activity distinguishes it from related arylcyclohexylamines, contributing to its unusual combination of stimulant and dissociative properties.

records.title: 3-MeO-PCP

tolerance.baseline_tolerance: 1-2 weeks under normal use patterns. However, following extended heavy use, residual tolerance may persist for weeks to months according to subjective reports.
tolerance.full_tolerance: Tolerance to the effects of 3-MeO-PCP develops rapidly with repeated use, often within a few days of consecutive dosing. At lighter doses, similar effects may persist for several days, particularly for non-dissociative effects such as stimulation, mood enhancement, and anxiolysis. However, the full dissociative effects associated with moderate to strong doses become progressively more difficult to achieve within just a few days of use. With substantial use patterns, such as daily dosing at low to moderate levels or weekly use of higher doses over weeks to months, some degree of tolerance may persist for weeks to months after complete cessation.

records.summary: 4-HO-DiPT is a psychedelic substance of the tryptamine class structurally related to psilocin.[cite:url-psychedelicreview-com-4-ho-dipt] First described in scientific literature by 1977 and later detailed by Alexander Shulgin in TiHKAL (1997)[citation-needed][citation-needed], it is distinguished by its unusually rapid onset, short duration, and steep dose-response curve.[citation-needed] Idiosyncratic physical effects such as muscle tremors and bodily malaise have been noted. It remains relatively uncommon with a limited history of human use and poorly understood toxicity.
records.title: 4-HO-DiPT

tolerance.baseline_tolerance: Approximately 7 days without further consumption
tolerance.full_tolerance: 4-HO-DiPT can cause tolerance to emerge very soon after ingestion.

routes.notes: Reported active doses vary widely between individuals; some report heavy effects near 17 mg while others report light effects at 30 mg, which has been attributed to differences in metabolism, batch quality, and salt form. Nausea is reported to be less prominent than with psilocybin mushrooms and may be reduced by dosing on an empty stomach.

Insufflated doses are similar to oral doses, with a more abrupt onset and shorter duration. Temporary nasal pain may occur. The faster onset increases the chance of intense, overwhelming, or disorienting effects early in the experience.

records.summary: 4-HO-MET is a synthetic psychedelic tryptamine first synthesized by Alexander Shulgin and documented in his 1997 book TiHKAL.[citation-needed] Structurally related to psilocin, it produces effects through serotonin receptor agonism.[citation-needed] Users typically describe it as more recreational than psilocybin mushrooms, characterized by vivid colorful visuals with a less mentally intense headspace. Reports of human use emerged in the late 2000s following its appearance on the research chemical market. Very little data exists regarding its toxicity profile.
records.title: 4-HO-MET

tolerance.baseline_tolerance: 7 days
tolerance.full_tolerance: Tolerance to the effects of 4-HO-MET develops almost immediately after ingestion. Notably, 4-HO-MET appears to be more amenable to redosing than many other psychedelics, with reports suggesting that taking an additional dose 1.5-2.5 hours after initial administration can restore or intensify effects without showing strong evidence of acute tolerance buildup.

routes.notes: Nausea may be reduced by taking the dose on an empty stomach; onset timing varies with the form taken and with stomach contents. Reported dose ranges are based on a small number of accounts and should be treated as tentative.

As with other fentanyl analogues, overdose carries a significant risk of respiratory depression. Extreme caution is strongly advised, and it should not be combined with other stimulants or depressants.

records.summary: 4-Methylmethylphenidate is a stimulant research chemical structurally related to methylphenidate. It appeared briefly on the market in mid-2015 following bans on ethylphenidate and other phenidates. The substance is reported to be slightly less potent than methylphenidate, with relatively low efficacy at blocking dopamine reuptake despite high binding affinity. It has been described as producing functional stimulation with limited recreational effects and was investigated as a potential substitute treatment for stimulant abuse.

routes.notes: This substance is commonly available in two salt forms: succinate and hydrochloride. The hydrochloride salt is roughly 10% more potent by weight, so doses should be adjusted downward accordingly when using this form.

records.summary: 5-MeO-DMT is a naturally occurring psychedelic of the tryptamine class, found in numerous plant species and in the venom of the Colorado River toad (Incilius alvarius).[citation-needed] It has been used in South American shamanic snuff preparations for centuries and was first identified in the plant Dictyoloma incanescens.[citation-needed] Reputed to produce among the most powerful and intense psychedelic states within its class,[citation-needed] it is considerably more potent by weight than its close relative DMT — a confusion between the two can lead to dangerous overdoses.

records.summary: 5-MeO-MiPT is a synthetic psychedelic and entactogenic substance of the tryptamine class. Its synthesis and human psychopharmacology were first published by Shulgin, Repke, and colleagues in 1985[citation-needed][citation-needed], with further documentation in Shulgin's 1997 book TiHKAL[cite:url-doubleblind-moxy]. The substance is characterized by its notably stimulating and body-oriented effects, including pronounced tactile and sexual enhancement[citation-needed], while generally producing fewer visual distortions than typical psychedelics.[cite:doi-10-1021-jm00145a007] It is almost exclusively obtained as a research chemical through online vendors.
records.title: 5-MeO-MiPT

tolerance.baseline_tolerance: 7 days of abstinence typically restores baseline sensitivity, though some sources suggest 5-7 days may be sufficient for most users.
tolerance.full_tolerance: Tolerance develops almost immediately after ingestion, though 5-MeO-MiPT appears to produce less tolerance than many other psychedelics. Some users report successful experiences on consecutive days, suggesting tolerance buildup is more moderate than typical for the class.

records.summary: 5-Methylethylone is a synthetic cathinone of the amphetamine and phenethylamine chemical classes, structurally related to ethylone. It has been sold as a designer drug and is reported to produce empathogenic, stimulant, and psychedelic effects, with a potency suspected to be slightly higher than ethylone. Very little data exists regarding its pharmacological properties, metabolism, or toxicity, making it a particularly poorly understood research chemical.

records.summary: 6-APB is a synthetic entactogen of the benzofuran class, structurally related to MDA.[citation-needed] First synthesized in 1993 by David E. Nichols as a potential non-neurotoxic alternative to MDMA, it did not see recreational use until over a decade later, when it was briefly sold on the research chemical market under the name "Benzofury."[citation-needed][citation-needed] Compared to MDMA, 6-APB is reported to produce stronger psychedelic and visual effects while retaining comparable entactogenic qualities.[citation-needed] Wide variability in dose response has been noted.

records.summary: α-PVP is a synthetic stimulant of the cathinone and pyrrolidinophenone classes, chemically related to prolintane and pyrovalerone. Originally patented by Boehringer Ingelheim in the 1960s but never marketed, it emerged as a recreational substance in the early 2010s. Known colloquially as flakka[cite:doi-10-3390-ijms21218185], α-PVP acts as a norepinephrine-dopamine reuptake inhibitor[cite:doi-10-3389-fphar-2025-1626692], producing powerful but short-lived effects comparable to methamphetamine and cocaine. It has been linked to numerous hospitalizations and deaths, with very limited toxicity data available[citation-needed].

records.summary: AL-LAD is a semi-synthetic psychedelic of the lysergamide class and a close structural analog of LSD. First described in scientific literature during the 1970s,[citation-needed] it was further investigated by Andrew J. Hoffman and David Nichols in 1984[citation-needed] and subsequently documented by Alexander Shulgin in TiHKAL.[cite:tihkal-al-lad] It entered the research chemical market around 2013 as a grey-market alternative to LSD.[citation-needed] Users often report enhanced visual activity with comparatively reduced cognitive intensity relative to LSD.[citation-needed]
records.title: AL-LAD

tolerance.half_tolerance: Approximately 5-7 days after ingestion, tolerance is estimated to reduce to roughly half of its peak level.

records.summary: Alcohol (ethanol) is a central nervous system depressant and one of the most widely used psychoactive substances in human history, with evidence of consumption dating back thousands of years.[citation-needed][citation-needed][citation-needed] It acts primarily through GABAergic mechanisms to produce anxiolytic, euphoriant, and sedative effects.[citation-needed][citation-needed] At common doses, alcohol reduces inhibition and increases sociability, while higher doses can cause blackouts and potentially fatal respiratory depression.[citation-needed][citation-needed] Despite its legal status in most countries, alcohol carries significant addiction potential and causes serious physical and psychological harm with chronic heavy use.[citation-needed][citation-needed]
records.title: Alcohol

tolerance.baseline_tolerance: Two or more consecutive alcohol-free days per week have been recommended to help prevent tolerance buildup and break dependence patterns.[citation-needed][citation-needed]
tolerance.full_tolerance: Tolerance develops with regular consumption of alcohol.[cite:elvig-2022-alcohol-tolerance][cite:pmc-acute-tolerance-binge] The rate of tolerance development varies between individuals and is influenced by drinking patterns and frequency of use.[citation-needed][citation-needed]

routes.notes: Potency is close to that of LSD, with sources reporting roughly 90 to 100 percent of LSD's potency; toxic dose and long-term effects are unstudied. Combination with MDMA is strongly synergistic and unpredictable, warranting markedly reduced doses of both.

records.summary: Amphetamine is a central nervous system stimulant[citation-needed] of the substituted phenethylamine class, first discovered in 1887 by Lazăr Edeleanu. records.summary: Brotizolam is a sedative-hypnotic of the thienotriazolodiazepine class, a benzodiazepine analog patented in 1974 and introduced into medical use in 1984.[citation-needed] It is prescribed for short-term treatment of severe insomnia in parts of Europe, Israel, and Japan. Brotizolam is notable for its exceptional potency and rapid elimination, producing effects comparable to triazolam and midazolam. As with other benzodiazepines, it carries risks of respiratory depression when combined with other depressants, as well as amnesia and habit formation.[citation-needed]

records.summary: Buprenorphine is a semisynthetic opioid of the morphinan class, first discovered in 1966 at Reckitt & Colman's research laboratories in England.[citation-needed] It functions as a partial mu-opioid receptor agonist with high binding affinity but lower intrinsic activity than full agonists such as heroin or methadone.[cite:nbk459126-buprenorphine-statpearls] Used clinically for both pain management and opioid addiction treatment,[cite:pmc-6585403-buprenorphine-overview] its slow receptor dissociation produces an unusually long duration of action.[cite:pande-2023-bup-complex] Respiratory depression from overdose is considered less likely than with other opioids.[citation-needed][citation-needed]

tolerance.full_tolerance: Tolerance to many effects develops with prolonged and repeated use, though the rate varies for different effects. Notably, tolerance to constipation-inducing effects develops particularly slowly. Some evidence suggests that buprenorphine tolerance may not develop as readily with chronic use compared to full opioid agonists, possibly due to its lack of delta-opioid agonism.

records.summary: Butyrfentanyl is a potent short-acting synthetic opioid and analog of fentanyl, possessing approximately one quarter of its parent compound's potency. It has no established clinical applications and is sold exclusively as a designer drug. One of the earliest references to this compound appears in documentation by The College on Problems of Drug Dependence. As with other fentanyl analogs, butyrfentanyl carries significant risk of respiratory depression and fatal overdose, demanding extreme caution.

routes.half_life_notes: Plasma concentrations typically peak between 30 minutes and 2 hours after ingestion, though food intake can slow absorption. Tobacco smoking accelerates caffeine clearance, potentially reducing the half-life by as much as half. During pregnancy, metabolism slows considerably, with the half-life extending to 15 hours or longer in the third trimester. Neonates metabolize caffeine far more slowly than adults: full-term infants have a half-life of approximately 8 hours, while premature infants may retain caffeine for up to 100 hours.

records.summary: Cannabis is a genus of flowering plant that has been used for thousands of years for medicinal, spiritual, and recreational purposes.[cite:breijyeh-2021-cannabis-toxins] Its primary psychoactive constituent is delta-9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC), though dozens of additional cannabinoids and terpenes contribute to its overall effects. It ranks among the most widely consumed recreational substances globally, behind only alcohol, caffeine, and tobacco. Its two principal species, sativa and indica, are recognized for producing distinct effect profiles.

tolerance.baseline_tolerance: Typically returns to baseline after 2-3 weeks of abstinence, though THC has been detected in heavy users up to 77 days after last use. Withdrawal symptoms in heavy users generally persist for 1-2 weeks.

Regular ingestion leads to increased tolerance to stimulating effects more rapidly than to relaxing effects due to the longer half-life of CBD (9 hours) compared to THC's stimulating effects (2-3 hours). Heavy users may require doses several times higher than cannabis-naive individuals to achieve comparable effects.

records.summary: Carisoprodol is a carbamate sedative-hypnotic and centrally acting muscle relaxant first approved for medical use in 1959.[citation-needed][citation-needed] Developed as an improvement upon meprobamate, it functions as a prodrug that is metabolized into meprobamate in the body.[citation-needed][citation-needed] Prescribed for the short-term treatment of musculoskeletal pain, it also possesses anxiolytic and hypnotic properties.[citation-needed] Its effects are often compared to barbiturates, and it has been largely supplanted by benzodiazepines due to safety concerns. records.summary: Clobazam is a long-acting benzodiazepine derivative belonging to the unique 1,5-benzodiazepine subclass, distinguishing it from the more common 1,4-benzodiazepines.[citation-needed][citation-needed] First synthesized in 1966[cite:nbk541043-statpearls-clobazam] and patented in 1968, it was initially marketed as an anxiolytic before gaining approval for epilepsy treatment in 1984.[citation-needed][citation-needed] Clobazam demonstrates a more favorable side-effect profile than older benzodiazepines, with notably less sedation and memory impairment,[citation-needed][citation-needed] and shows a distinct addictive potential compared to its 1,4-benzodiazepine counterparts.[citation-needed]

tolerance.full_tolerance: Tolerance to the therapeutic and anticonvulsant effects of clobazam develops with continued therapy. This differential tolerance pattern is characteristic of benzodiazepines and may render long-term therapy less effective for epilepsy management.

records.summary: Clonazepam is a long-acting benzodiazepine[cite:ncbi-books-nbk556010] that produces primarily anxiolytic effects alongside anticonvulsant[citation-needed], sedative, muscle relaxant, and hypnotic properties. Patented in 1960 and first marketed in the United States by Roche in 1975, it is widely prescribed for the treatment of panic disorder[citation-needed], anxiety disorders, and seizures[citation-needed]. Now available as a generic medication, it remains one of the most commonly prescribed benzodiazepines, with millions of prescriptions written internationally each year.

tolerance.baseline_tolerance: Typically returns to baseline within 7-14 days following cessation, although individuals with extended histories of regular use may require considerably longer periods for complete tolerance reset.
tolerance.full_tolerance: Tolerance to sedative-hypnotic effects can emerge quickly, often after only several days of uninterrupted use. Tolerance to anticonvulsant effects may also develop with prolonged administration.
tolerance.half_tolerance: 7-14 days after cessation of use, though this may take significantly longer in cases of prolonged or intensive use.

routes.notes: Extremely potent; doses as small as 0.5 mg can produce strong sedation and amnesia, and doses above 0.5 mg can cause benzodiazepine overdose in some individuals. Onset may be delayed, with some users feeling little or nothing until 1-2 hours after administration; redosing is inadvisable at any point. Vendors often sell 500 µg products despite this exceeding a common dose.

records.summary: Clonazolam is a highly potent depressant of the triazolobenzodiazepine class[cite:who-ecdd-clonazolam-2020], structurally related to both clonazepam and alprazolam[cite:who-ecdd-clonazolam-2020]. First synthesized in 1971, it was never marketed pharmaceutically[cite:who-ecdd-clonazolam-2020] and has been available as a research chemical since the mid-2000s. It is considered to pose higher risks than many other designer benzodiazepines due to its exceptional potency[citation-needed], with strong sedation and amnesia[citation-needed] reported at very low doses. Blackouts and dependence are frequently reported concerns.

records.summary: Cocaine is a tropane alkaloid stimulant derived from the leaves of coca plants native to South America.[citation-needed] It has a long history of medical use as a topical anesthetic owing to its intrinsic vasoconstrictor properties and voltage-gated sodium channel inhibition[citation-needed][citation-needed], though its high abuse potential[citation-needed] has largely supplanted this role. Cocaine functions as a serotonin–norepinephrine–dopamine reuptake inhibitor[cite:doi-10-3390-toxins14040278], producing euphoria and heightened alertness.[cite:doi-10-3390-toxins14040278] It is notably cardiotoxic[citation-needed] and carries a significant potential for compulsive redosing[citation-needed] and addiction.[citation-needed]

tolerance.full_tolerance: Tolerance to the euphoric effects of cocaine develops rapidly, potentially after even a single dose. The short duration of action encourages repeated dosing within a session, which accelerates tolerance development. Users often report diminishing returns with consecutive uses, requiring higher doses to achieve initial effects.

routes.notes: Most individuals experience a ceiling effect for both analgesic and euphoric properties in the range of 300–500 mg, though some may find this threshold extends to approximately 600 mg due to individual variation. Doses beyond this point primarily increase the risk and severity of adverse effects rather than producing proportionally greater desired effects.

routes.half_life_notes:
Curated community references support only the two stored oral rows. Erowid's Basics summary states that oral effects take 15 to 90 minutes to begin, depending on experience and stomach contents.[cite:url-erowid-17c512] PsychonautWiki's route table gives oral total duration as 3 to 4 hours.[cite:url-psychonautwiki-4dc858] Neither establishes come-up, peak, offset, or after-effects.

A 1957 World Health Organization synthesis reported that, in 126 desomorphine cases treated for postoperative pain, pain relief averaged 2 hours 25 minutes per dose and sleep averaged 2 hours 7 minutes per dose; the accessible excerpt does not identify the administration route for that comparison.[cite:pmid-13511135]

Those clinical endpoints are not equivalent to onset, come-up, peak, offset, total subjective duration, or elimination half-life. Human pharmacokinetic studies and a measured human half-life were not identified, and the California Poison Control page supplies only comparative fast-onset and short-duration language, so no additional stages should be populated.[cite:url-ojp-31c87e][cite:url-calpoison-2766c6]

records.title: Dextroamphetamine

tolerance.full_tolerance: Tolerance develops rapidly with repeated use over short periods, leading to diminished effects. The rate of tolerance development may vary between different effects of the substance.

fifth_plateau.effects: STRONGLY DISCOURAGED. Achieved through repeated dosing (2.5-7.5 mg/kg every 3 hours over 9-12 hours), not a single dose. Causes dysphoria, delirium, psychosis, and anxiety. Neurotoxic with high risk of serotonin syndrome. Can last 1-4 days. White noted that over half of those who reached Sigma found it extremely unpleasant and would not repeat the experience.

first_plateau.effects: Mild euphoria, increased music appreciation, stimulation, time distortion, pupil dilation. Often described as a "drunk" feeling with a shift in thinking perspective and enhanced tactile sensation.

fourth_plateau.effects: Complete dissociation similar to a K-hole, external hallucinations, full amnesia common, out-of-body experiences. Very dangerous with high risk of injury and overdose.

plateau_dosing.notes: The plateau classification system originated in "The DXM FAQ" by William E. White, initially published in 1995. This framework divides DXM experiences into distinct stages based on weight-adjusted dosage (mg/kg) and continues to be a commonly referenced model for describing dose-dependent effects. This dosage scale applies to DXM HBr, adjust dosage accordingly on molecular mass.

second_plateau.effects: Stronger euphoria, visual disconnection, sedation, spatial disorientation, perception of bodily lightness, mild closed-eye visuals. Considered the most recreational plateau. Movement becomes difficult.

third_plateau.effects: Full dissociative experience with strong sedation, memory suppression, ego death, internal and auditory hallucinations. Highly introspective with possible anxiety, nausea during comeup, and post-trip amnesia.

records.summary: Dextromethorphan (DXM) is a morphinan-class dissociative commonly found in over-the-counter cough suppressants.[citation-needed][citation-needed] First approved by the FDA in 1957, it acts primarily as a prodrug, with most dissociative effects mediated by its metabolite dextrorphan through NMDA receptor antagonism. Despite its structural similarity to opioids like codeine, dextromethorphan lacks significant mu-opioid receptor activity.[cite:ncbi-statpearls-dextromethorphan] Its widespread availability in household cold medicines has made it one of the most accessible dissociatives, contributing to its prevalence as a recreationally misused substance.[citation-needed]

Some users report an irreversible, permanent tolerance that develops over extended periods of heavy use, potentially correlating with cumulative lifetime doses. Anecdotal reports suggest a threshold around 50 uses after which the characteristic effects may be permanently diminished, though the mechanism remains unclear.

routes.notes: Doses of 5 mg or more can cause significant deterioration in alertness alongside increased sleepiness. In elderly patients the smallest effective amount is recommended, starting at 2-2.5 mg once or twice daily and increasing gradually only as needed and tolerated.

records.summary: Dihydrocodeine is a semi-synthetic opioid analgesic[cite:dailymed-dihydrocodeine-bitartrate-acetaminophen-caffeine-f3ddb645] of the morphinan class. Developed in Germany in 1908 and first marketed in 1911, it was originally created during efforts to find more effective antitussive medications to curb the spread of airborne diseases like tuberculosis. Slightly more potent than codeine, it is prescribed for moderate to severe pain[citation-needed], dyspnea, and cough suppression. It is commonly sold in combination formulations containing paracetamol[citation-needed] or aspirin[cite:dailymed-aspirin-caffeine-dihydrocodeine], which pose additional overdose risks[citation-needed][citation-needed] if not accounted for.

Above 500 mg, a deliriant state may emerge, characterized by vivid visual and auditory hallucinations. Doses between these ranges often produce dysphoria and significant discomfort. Amounts approaching or exceeding 2 grams carry serious risk of fatal overdose, especially in combination with other stimulants or MAOIs.

Pediatric and adolescent populations demonstrate intermediate values, with studies reporting half-lives in the range of 5-9 hours.

records.summary: DOM is a psychedelic amphetamine of the DOx family[citation-needed][citation-needed], first synthesized by Alexander Shulgin in 1963[citation-needed] and later documented in his 1991 book PiHKAL[citation-needed]. It gained notoriety during the 1967 Summer of Love in San Francisco, where high-dosed tablets caused hospitalizations due to its characteristically slow onset and extremely long duration[cite:baggott-2023-stp]. Shulgin considered it one of his "magical half-dozen" — his personal favorite compounds. It produces stimulant effects at lower doses and hallucinogenic effects at higher doses[citation-needed][citation-needed].
records.title: DOM

tolerance.baseline_tolerance: Approximately 7 days of abstinence
cross_tolerance: Psychedelics (all serotonergic psychedelics will have reduced effects following DOM consumption)
tolerance.full_tolerance: Tolerance to the effects of DOM develops almost immediately after ingestion. Clinical studies have demonstrated that with daily administration over three consecutive days, subjective effects diminish dramatically—ranging from 'moderately strong' responses to complete absence of effects by the third day, with one subject actually sleeping through the experience.

routes.notes: Oral bioavailability is relatively low, and individual responses can vary considerably. The onset of effects is influenced by whether the stomach is empty or contains food. Community reference timings for this route are contextual rather than clinical: PsychonautWiki lists oral total 2–4 hours, onset 20–60 minutes, and after-effects 2–3 hours, and does not establish come-up, peak, or offset values.[cite:url-psychonautwiki-13ba30]

Nasal administration results in rapid absorption but is commonly associated with considerable irritation and a burning sensation. Community reference timings for this route are contextual rather than clinical: PsychonautWiki lists insufflated total 3–5 hours, onset 5–20 minutes, peak 30–45 minutes, and after-effects 2–4 hours.[cite:url-psychonautwiki-13ba30]

This is the most sensitive administration route. The rapid onset and intensity of effects may be psychologically overwhelming for some users. Community reference timings for this route are contextual rather than clinical and disagree between sources: PsychonautWiki lists smoked total 30–90 minutes, onset 0–1 minutes, and after-effects 2–4 hours, and TripSit also lists 30–90 minutes total, while Erowid and The Drug Classroom list 30–60 minutes.[cite:url-psychonautwiki-13ba30][cite:url-erowid-5d2139][cite:url-tripbot-a34c4d][cite:url-thedrugclassroom-22c225]

Clinical research has employed doses of 15–30 mg as a therapeutic adjunct, while intensive peak experiences have been studied using 75–125 mg. Community reference timings for this route are contextual rather than clinical: Erowid lists onset 2–10 minutes, duration 3–4 hours, and normal after-effects 2–4 hours; TripSit lists the same values; and The Drug Classroom lists onset 2–10 minutes and total 3–4 hours, qualifying its timelines as average common-dose durations. These summaries do not replace the 15–30 mg clinical-study timeline.[cite:url-erowid-5d2139][cite:url-tripbot-a34c4d][cite:url-thedrugclassroom-22c225]

When vaporized, DPT produces a rapid onset comparable to smoking, with a relatively short overall duration of effects. Community references do not establish vaporized inhalation as a route distinct from smoking, and their smoked or vaporized totals vary by source from 30–60 minutes at Erowid and The Drug Classroom to 30–90 minutes at PsychonautWiki and TripSit.[cite:url-psychonautwiki-13ba30][cite:url-erowid-5d2139][cite:url-tripbot-a34c4d][cite:url-thedrugclassroom-22c225]

routes.half_life_notes: In a double-blind psychotherapy study of 18 hospitalized men with alcoholism, 15–30 mg intramuscular DPT usually produced observable effects within 5–15 minutes. Effects reached peak intensity within about 20 minutes, remained fairly constant for the next 45–60 minutes, began to wane after about 90 minutes, and were almost completely resolved by two hours. Some participants reported increased introspection or reflectiveness for several additional hours. These timings apply only to the studied low-dose intramuscular sessions and should not be generalized to other routes, populations, or doses.[cite:doi-10-1001-archpsyc-1973-01750360047006]

records.summary: DPT is a synthetic psychedelic of the tryptamine class[cite:doi-10-1016-j-pbb-2007-09-007], closely related to DMT. First described in the scientific literature by the late 1950s, it was subsequently investigated during the 1970s as an adjunct in therapeutic settings for alcoholism[citation-needed] and to facilitate peak experiences in terminal cancer patients. DPT is noted for producing hallucinogenic effects comparable in intensity to DMT, though with greater unpredictability and wider individual variation in response at any given dose.

records.summary: Ephedrine is a naturally occurring stimulant alkaloid found in plants of the Ephedra genus, with a long history of use in traditional Chinese medicine.[citation-needed] First isolated in 1885,[cite:lee-2011-ephedra-history] it is a substituted amphetamine that acts as a sympathomimetic agent.[citation-needed] Ephedrine is used clinically as a decongestant, bronchodilator, and to treat hypotension during anesthesia,[citation-needed] and is listed on the WHO's List of Essential Medicines.[cite:who-eml-2023] Though structurally related to methamphetamine, its central nervous system effects are considerably less potent.[cite:pmc-cns-stimulants-sport]

routes.notes: Strong tolerance develops rapidly, requiring progressively larger doses to achieve the same effects; tolerance is reported to return to baseline after 1 to 2 weeks of abstinence.

records.summary: Eszopiclone is a nonbenzodiazepine hypnotic of the cyclopyrrolone class and the active S-stereoisomer of zopiclone.[citation-needed] It belongs to the family of drugs colloquially known as "Z-drugs." First approved by the FDA in 2004 for the treatment of insomnia,[citation-needed] it is notable for being one of few hypnotic sedatives approved for long-term use.[citation-needed] Eszopiclone enhances GABAergic neurotransmission in a manner similar to yet distinct from benzodiazepines[citation-needed] and is considered habit-forming.[cite:url-dailymed-nlm-nih-gov-druginfo-cfm]

records.summary: Etizolam is a depressant substance of the thienodiazepine class, structurally related to benzodiazepines but distinguished by a thiophene ring replacing the characteristic benzene ring.[citation-needed] While prescribed medically for anxiety, insomnia, and panic disorder in some countries,[citation-needed] it has gained widespread use as a research chemical and is commonly employed as a substitute for pharmaceutical benzodiazepines such as alprazolam and diazepam.[citation-needed] Like benzodiazepines, it carries significant habit-forming potential.[cite:pmid-7671959-pmc]

tolerance.full_tolerance: Tolerance to sedative-hypnotic effects can appear after only several days of uninterrupted use. Notably, some research suggests etizolam may have a reduced liability to induce tolerance compared to classic benzodiazepines; in controlled studies comparing etizolam with lorazepam, tolerance to anticonvulsant effects developed with lorazepam but not etizolam. Paradoxically, one clinical trial found etizolam became more effective over time for treating generalized anxiety disorder, suggesting a possible reverse tolerance phenomenon for anxiolytic effects.

Insufflated onset and total duration are curated PsychonautWiki community-reference estimates; no controlled clinical validation was identified.[cite:url-psychonautwiki-240fa8]

LAZANDA nasal spray reaches a median Tmax of 15 to 21 minutes after a single dose, which is formulation plasma timing rather than subjective effect duration.[cite:url-dailymed-4ec42e]

Onset of 15–30 minutes and total duration of 1–4 hours are curated PsychonautWiki community-reference estimates for sublingual use; no direct controlled validation was identified, and they are not derived from SUBSYS Tmax or half-life.[cite:url-psychonautwiki-240fa8]

The US SUBSYS label reports a terminal half-life of 5 to 12 hours after sublingual-spray administration. That is an elimination measure for that named formulation, not a subjective effect duration and not a value for every sublingual or buccal fentanyl product.[cite:url-dailymed-6c612c]

Transdermal onset and total duration are curated PsychonautWiki community-reference estimates.[cite:url-psychonautwiki-240fa8]

TripSit instead labels patch come-up as 20 to 60 minutes and patch duration as 24 to 72 hours; the two community sources disagree and their ranges must not be averaged.[cite:url-wiki-5bad1a]

Transdermal-system plasma concentrations generally level off between 12 and 24 hours and stay there for the remainder of the 72-hour application period, which is formulation kinetics rather than effect duration.[cite:url-dailymed-7b3ad6]

records.summary: Fentanyl is a synthetic opioid[cite:cdc-fentanyl-2025] of the anilidopiperidine class first synthesized by Paul Janssen in 1960[cite:stanley-2014-fentanyl-story] and approved for medical use in the United States in 1968[cite:stanley-2014-fentanyl-story]. records.summary: Furanylfentanyl is a potent synthetic opioid analgesic of the anilinopiperidine class and a structural analogue of fentanyl.[citation-needed][citation-needed] Classified as a research chemical, it has extremely limited pharmacological and toxicological documentation available. It is thought to be somewhat less potent and shorter-acting than butyrfentanyl. Due to the scarcity of reliable information and its high potency, exercising extreme caution with this substance is strongly recommended.
records.title: Furanylfentanyl

routes.bioavailability_notes:
Absorption relies on a saturable amino acid transporter in the intestines, meaning the body can only absorb a limited amount at a time
At 100 mg per dose, approximately 80% reaches the bloodstream; at 300 mg this drops to about 60%, at 800 mg to about 34%, and at 1600 mg to about 27%
routes.notes: Gabapentin exhibits dose-dependent oral bioavailability that decreases at higher amounts owing to saturation of intestinal amino acid transporters. Splitting a total dose into smaller portions taken at 30- to 45-minute intervals can improve absorption relative to a single large dose. Tolerance to the anxiolytic effects typically develops during continuous use and generally resolves within one to two weeks after discontinuation.

routes.half_life_notes: Peak plasma concentration is typically reached within 2–3 hours of oral administration. Because gabapentin is eliminated almost entirely through the kidneys, its half-life increases substantially in individuals with impaired renal function—extending to roughly 52 hours in cases of severe kidney impairment.

records.summary: Gabapentin is a depressant substance of the gabapentinoid class and a structural analogue of the neurotransmitter GABA[citation-needed]. Originally developed in the 1970s to treat epilepsy, it was first approved in the United States in 1993[citation-needed] and is now widely prescribed for neuropathic pain[citation-needed], postherpetic neuralgia, and partial-onset seizures[cite:neurontin-dailymed-label]. Its anxiolytic, sedative, and mildly euphoriant properties have led to recreational use[citation-needed], though tolerance is known to develop rapidly.
records.title: Gabapentin

tolerance.baseline_tolerance: Tolerance returns to baseline within 7-14 days after cessation of use.
tolerance.full_tolerance: Tolerance to anxiolytic and euphoric effects can build rapidly with repeated dosing, sometimes after several days in a row. Reported recreational benefits may fade quickly, with repeat doses producing much smaller returns even during the same session.

routes.bioavailability_notes: Greater lipophilicity than GHB allows faster absorption and higher bioavailability by mouth
routes.notes: GBL is highly caustic and must be diluted thoroughly in a non-alcoholic liquid before ingestion to avoid injury to the mouth, throat, and stomach lining. Amounts above 2 ml commonly produce deep sedation or unconsciousness. Individual response varies widely; compared with GHB, GBL acts more rapidly and with greater potency, though its effects are shorter-lived. First time users are recommended to start lower as lactonase enzyme levels vary between individuals, which can produce unpredictable responses.

records.summary: GBL is a synthetic depressant of the lactone chemical class that functions as a prodrug for GHB[citation-needed], producing powerful euphoric and disinhibiting effects comparable to alcohol intoxication. It is widely available as an industrial solvent and cleaning agent.[citation-needed] GBL is a strong acid that corrodes mucous membranes and must be heavily diluted in a non-alcoholic beverage before oral consumption. It also dissolves most plastics, requiring glass or high-density polyethylene containers for storage.
records.title: GBL

tolerance.baseline_tolerance: Tolerance returns to baseline within 7-14 days after cessation of use. Abrupt discontinuation following several days or longer of steady dosing may necessitate gradual dose reduction to minimize withdrawal-related neurotoxicity.
cross_tolerance: Other GABAergic depressants (alcohol, phenibut, baclofen, and other GABA-B agonists)
tolerance.full_tolerance: Tolerance to sedative-hypnotic effects develops quickly, usually over several days of uninterrupted use. GBL is believed to produce dependence more rapidly than longer-duration depressants, and withdrawal effects are reported to escalate faster than with GHB itself.

routes.notes: Doses of 3 grams or more commonly produce heavy sedation, while amounts exceeding 3.5 grams carry a significant risk of sudden loss of consciousness. Because the margin between desired effects and dangerous overdose is narrow, precise measurement with calibrated equipment is critical. If onset is slower than expected, allow a minimum of two hours before considering any additional dose.

records.summary: GHB is a depressant that occurs naturally in the human body. First synthesized in the 1920s, it has seen varied use as an anesthetic, a bodybuilding supplement, and eventually a recreational club drug by the late 1990s. It is known for producing euphoric, disinhibiting, and sedative effects. GHB carries notable risks due to inconsistent concentrations in commonly sold liquid form and dangerous interactions with other depressants.
records.title: GHB

tolerance.full_tolerance: Regular use can lead to physical dependence, particularly with chronic high-dose consumption involving multiple daily doses. The development of tolerance appears to occur alongside dependence formation.

records.summary: βH-2C-B is a largely undocumented psychoactive substance presumed to be a structural analog of 2C-B based on its naming convention. Its psychoactive and chemical classifications remain formally unestablished. Virtually no reliable information exists regarding its pharmacology, subjective effects, or safety profile. Due to this extreme scarcity of data, it should be approached with considerable caution, as its risks remain entirely uncharacterized.

records.summary: Heroin (diacetylmorphine[citation-needed]) is a semi-synthetic opioid of the morphinan class derived from morphine[citation-needed], a natural product of the opium poppy[citation-needed]. First synthesized by a British chemist in 1874[citation-needed] and later commercialized by Bayer in 1898[citation-needed], it is among the most notorious substances of abuse worldwide. Heroin is highly addictive[citation-needed] and exists in forms ranging from white or brown powder to black tar[cite:nida-research-topics-heroin], with street purity varying dramatically from as low as 5% to as high as 95%.
records.title: Heroin

tolerance.baseline_tolerance: 1-2 weeks

tolerance.full_tolerance: With sustained repeated heroin use, many effects become less responsive. Tolerance does not develop at the same pace for every effect; constipation-related tolerance is especially slow compared with other effects. As a result, users may need progressively higher doses to obtain effects that previously occurred at lower doses.

records.summary: HXE (3-HO-2'-Oxo-PCE) is a novel dissociative substance of the arylcyclohexylamine class that produces ketamine-like effects. Structurally related to methoxetamine, ketamine, and PCE, it is distinguished by a hydroxy group on the phenyl ring in place of the methoxy group found in MXE.[citation-needed] HXE first became available on the research chemical market in late 2020 after years of synthesis difficulties. Very limited data exists regarding its pharmacology, metabolism, and toxicity in humans.

routes.half_life_notes: The elimination half-life averages approximately 3.8 hours, although some reports indicate values ranging from 7 to 9 hours. Immediate-release formulations typically reach peak plasma concentrations within 30 to 60 minutes, whereas extended-release preparations achieve peak levels at 14 to 16 hours. Individual variation in metabolic enzyme activity can influence the rate of elimination. Notably, inhibition of CYP3A4 may substantially prolong the half-life.

records.summary: Hydromorphone is a semisynthetic opioid of the morphinan class, derived as a hydrogenated ketone of morphine. First introduced to the mass market in 1926 under the brand name Dilaudid,[citation-needed][citation-needed] it is prescribed for the management of moderate to severe pain.[citation-needed] Hydromorphone is notably more potent than morphine[citation-needed] and carries a high potential for addiction and dependence.[citation-needed] It has low oral bioavailability[cite:dailymed-dilaudid-oral-d6b40e39] and is most commonly administered intravenously in clinical settings.
records.title: Hydromorphone

tolerance.baseline_tolerance: After a period without opioid use, fatal overdose risk rises sharply because physical tolerance to respiratory and other depressant effects is reduced. For someone resuming use after extended abstinence, a much smaller fraction of the previous usual dose is safer. Environmental context may also influence tolerance, as studies suggest familiar drug-associated settings can provide some conditioned tolerance.
tolerance.full_tolerance: Prolonged repeated hydromorphone use can produce tolerance to many effects, including therapeutic benefits. Once tolerance develops, comparable effects may require larger doses. The pace is effect-specific, and constipation-related tolerance tends to appear more slowly than tolerance to other opioid effects.

records.summary: Hydroxyzine is a first-generation antihistamine of the diphenylmethane and piperazine classes, first developed in 1956.[citation-needed] Primarily prescribed for allergic conditions such as itchiness and urticaria,[citation-needed] it also exhibits anxiolytic and sedative properties, making it useful for treating generalized anxiety disorder and insomnia.[citation-needed][citation-needed] Hydroxyzine is additionally employed to reduce nausea[cite:dailymed-hcl-injection-8af7e5ce] and has been used to potentiate opioid analgesia while diminishing opioid-related side effects like itchiness.[citation-needed][citation-needed]

records.summary: Ibogaine is a naturally occurring indole alkaloid primarily derived from the root bark of Tabernanthe iboga, a plant native to Central and West Africa.[citation-needed] It has been used for centuries within the Bwiti religion of Gabon for initiation rites and spiritual communion.[citation-needed] Ibogaine produces psychedelic and dissociative effects often described as dream-like and frequently unpleasant.[citation-needed] Since the late 20th century, it has gained significant attention as an experimental treatment for opioid dependence, with clinics established worldwide.[cite:doi-10-3390-molecules20022208][citation-needed]

records.summary: Isomethadone is a synthetic opioid analgesic structurally related to methadone. As with other opioids, it carries a risk of habit formation and respiratory depression.

records.summary: Ketamine is a dissociative anesthetic[cite:doi-10-1007-s43440-021-00232-4] of the arylcyclohexylamine class, developed in the early 1960s by Parke-Davis Laboratories[citation-needed] as a replacement for phencyclidine (PCP). Widely employed in both human and veterinary medicine[citation-needed], it is considered the archetypal dissociative substance. Recreational use became widespread through the 1990s rave and nightclub scenes. More recently, it has attracted significant clinical interest for its ability to rapidly alleviate treatment-resistant depression[cite:doi-10-1007-s43440-021-00232-4] and suicidal ideation[cite:doi-10-1007-s43440-021-00232-4].
records.title: Ketamine

tolerance.baseline_tolerance: Tolerance may decline after abstinence, but the time needed for a full reset depends on individual physiology, amount and frequency of use, and total exposure duration. Some users report needing a month or longer for tolerance to return to baseline. Dissociatives such as ketamine are also reported to produce long-lasting or permanent tolerance ('permatolerance') that builds gradually apart from ordinary tolerance, with many chronic users saying they need much higher doses to reach dissociation even after long breaks.
tolerance.full_tolerance: Tolerance to dissociative, euphoric, hallucinogenic, and psychotomimetic effects can develop after sustained repeated use. The pace varies widely between individuals: some people report tolerance after one night of heavy use, while others need weeks of regular consumption before noticing it. High-dose nonmedical ketamine use can readily produce tolerance to its main effects.

routes.notes:
Lithium is a prescription medicine, and these figures are label-based medical information for adults rather than a self-dosing guide. For bipolar I disorder, the cited U.S. immediate-release capsule label gives a starting dose of 300 mg by mouth three times daily. For an acute manic or mixed episode the usual adult dose is 600 mg two or three times daily, titrated to a 12-hour serum concentration of 0.8–1.2 mEq/L. For maintenance the usual adult dose is 300–600 mg two or three times daily, titrated to a 12-hour serum concentration of 0.8–1.0 mEq/L.[cite:dailymed-licarbonate-63b3790f]

Lithium has a narrow therapeutic range. Dosing must be individualized using clinical assessment and serum concentrations, because toxicity can occur near therapeutic concentrations.[cite:dailymed-licarbonate-63b3790f] Renal impairment, pregnancy and the postpartum period, geriatric use, and pediatric use each require their own clinical context and are not covered by these adult figures.

records.summary: MDMA is a classical entactogen of the substituted amphetamine class[citation-needed], first developed in 1912 by the pharmaceutical company Merck.[citation-needed] It remained largely obscure until the 1970s, when it gained recognition in underground psychotherapy circles before spreading into nightlife and rave culture. Now one of the most popular recreational drugs worldwide, it is known for producing strong feelings of empathy, emotional closeness, and stimulation.[citation-needed] Tablets sold as "ecstasy" frequently contain adulterants or other substances entirely.[citation-needed]

tolerance.baseline_tolerance: Approximately 2.5 months after a single use in the absence of further consumption. A complete drug-free period of 6 days has been shown to reverse tolerance established through consecutive daily dosing. Most harm reduction guidance recommends waiting 1-3 months between uses, with 4-6 weeks considered an absolute minimum to allow adequate serotonin restoration.
tolerance.full_tolerance: Tolerance to MDMA's effects develops unusually quickly compared to many other substances. In controlled observations, daily administration of 120-160 mg resulted in complete loss of subjective effects by the fifth or sixth day, with only mild pupil dilation remaining. A notable phenomenon described as 'losing the magic' occurs with repeated use, where the characteristic empathogenic and prosocial effects diminish substantially while stimulant and euphoric properties may persist. Some users report this degradation after as few as 10 experiences, while others maintain full effects through dozens or even hundreds of uses. The empathogenic qualities appear particularly susceptible to tolerance, often fading before other effects.

records.summary: MET is a lesser-known synthetic psychedelic of the tryptamine class,[citation-needed] structurally related to DMT.[cite:doi-10-3390-ijms21239279] It produces powerful, short-lived psychedelic effects characterized by rapid onset and progressive stages. When smoked or vaporized, its effects have been compared to those of DMT but with a more grounded headspace and reduced subjective intensity. Very little data exists regarding its pharmacology, metabolism, or toxicity, and it has only been available through online research chemical vendors since mid-2016.

routes.notes: Methadone is characterized by an extended and highly variable half-life. Peak effects and complete absorption may be significantly delayed, so additional doses should not be taken within several hours of the initial dose. In clinical opioid agonist therapy settings, typical maintenance doses range from 40 to 100 mg per day.

routes.half_life_notes: The mean elimination half-life of methadone is roughly 22 hours, though individual variation is substantial—documented cases range from as short as 4 hours to as long as 190 hours. This wide variability is largely attributable to genetic polymorphisms affecting hepatic cytochrome P450 enzymes, particularly CYP3A4, CYP2B6, and CYP2D6. Opioid-tolerant individuals tend to clear the drug more rapidly (approximately 24 hours) than opioid-naive individuals (approximately 55 hours). Methadone's high lipid solubility also contributes to its prolonged systemic presence. Following oral administration, peak plasma concentrations typically occur within 1 to 7.5 hours.

Opioid-tolerant individuals may metabolize methadone more quickly (~24 hours) compared to opioid-naive individuals (~55 hours)
High fat solubility contributes to the drug's prolonged presence in the body
Peak plasma concentrations are reached between 1 and 7.5 hours after oral dosing

records.summary: Methamphetamine is a potent synthetic stimulant of the substituted amphetamine class. First synthesized in 1893 by Japanese chemist Nagayoshi Nagai, it saw widespread use during World War II to combat fatigue and was later prescribed for obesity and attention deficit disorder under the brand name Desoxyn.[citation-needed] Because it is more lipid-soluble than amphetamine, it enters the brain faster. Methamphetamine carries a significant risk of addiction and remains widely used as a street drug.[citation-needed]
records.title: Methamphetamine

tolerance.baseline_tolerance: 1-2 weeks in the absence of further consumption, though recovery for heavy users can take significantly longer, potentially years for full normalization of reward sensitivity.
tolerance.full_tolerance: Repeated methamphetamine use over time can produce rapid tolerance, causing users to need larger doses for similar effects. Euphoria fades especially quickly, often becoming much weaker after the first few uses or after several doses in succession. Subjective effects such as empathy enhancement and openness also tend to vanish early, once initial exposures or broader tolerance have occurred. Chronically tolerant users may require dosages 2-3 times higher than amounts effective for naive users.

This extended half-life may lead to drug accumulation with repeated dosing.

records.summary: Methaqualone is a sedative-hypnotic depressant of the quinazolinone class.[citation-needed] Its sedative properties were first identified by researchers in the 1950s, and it was patented in the United States in 1962. During the 1970s, it saw widespread medical use for insomnia and muscle relaxation, as well as significant recreational popularity within the counterculture and disco scenes. Though largely discontinued as a pharmaceutical, it continues to be produced clandestinely, particularly in South Africa.[citation-needed] Illicit methaqualone products are often adulterated, sometimes with other CNS depressants.
records.title: Methaqualone

tolerance.baseline_tolerance: 1-2 weeks of abstinence in the absence of further consumption. Avoiding tolerance buildup generally requires spacing doses by several days up to about a week.
tolerance.full_tolerance: Tolerance to sedative-hypnotic effects develops quickly, often after only a few days of repeated dosing. Physical dependence can develop within about two weeks when moderate doses are used every day. Tolerance to euphoric effects appears to develop faster than tolerance to respiratory depression, substantially increasing overdose risk when users raise doses to regain earlier subjective effects.
tolerance.half_tolerance: Approximately 3-7 days after cessation of use.

routes.notes: The stimulant effects can feel subtle initially, creating a risk of overdose through redosing. Overdose may cause heart palpitations, gastrointestinal upset, restlessness, and sleep disturbances.

It entered recreational drug markets around 2010 as a research chemical and legal high. Methiopropamine is generally characterized as a functional stimulant with limited euphoric properties.

records.summary: Methoxetamine is a dissociative substance of the arylcyclohexylamine class, structurally related to ketamine and PCP.[citation-needed][citation-needed] It was intentionally designed as a possible therapy for phantom limb syndrome and first appeared on grey markets in late 2010. MXE was noted for its ketamine-like dissociative effects with a pronounced psychedelic character. Once widely available as a research chemical, it is now considered largely extinct due to global bans on its production.

records.summary: Methoxyacetyl-fentanyl is a highly potent synthetic opioid and fentanyl analogue classified as a depressant research chemical. Like other fentanyl analogues, it carries significant habit-forming potential. Its high potency presents serious overdose risks, as even minor dosing errors can prove fatal. Very limited information is available regarding its pharmacology and safety profile, making it an especially dangerous substance to use without proper harm reduction precautions.
records.title: Methoxyacetyl-Fentanyl

binding_sites.affinity: Lower potency than ketamine; precise affinity not established

records.summary: Methoxyketamine is a dissociative research chemical of the arylcyclohexylamine class and a structural analogue of ketamine. It is reported to produce dissociative and anesthetic effects comparable to those of ketamine, though at a slightly lower potency. The substance is considered extremely rare, with very limited availability and documentation. As with other dissociatives in its class, it may carry habit-forming potential.
records.title: Methoxyketamine

routes.notes: This substance has been associated with a high rate of seizures. The margin between doses producing sedative effects and those triggering convulsions is reported to be narrow, warranting extreme caution with dosing.

records.summary: Methylmethaqualone is a depressant research chemical and a more potent structural analogue of methaqualone. It is characterized by a comparatively short duration of action relative to its parent compound. The substance carries significant safety concerns, as it is suspected to be neurotoxic and has been reported to produce proconvulsive effects. Due to its limited research history and potential for harm, it should be approached with considerable caution.
records.title: Methylmethaqualone

records.summary: Midazolam is a short-acting depressant of the benzodiazepine class, specifically an imidazobenzodiazepine.[citation-needed][citation-needed] Patented in 1974 and adopted for medical use in 1982, it is distinguished from other benzodiazepines by its rapid onset and brief duration of action.[citation-needed][citation-needed] It is widely used clinically for procedural sedation, anesthesia, seizure management, and acute agitation,[citation-needed][citation-needed] and is included on the World Health Organization's List of Essential Medicines.[cite:who-eml-essentialmeds] Like all benzodiazepines, it carries a risk of dependence with repeated use.[citation-needed]

tolerance.full_tolerance: Tolerance develops rapidly with continuous use. In intensive care settings, midazolam infusions may induce tolerance in a matter of days. With therapeutic use, benzodiazepine dependence occurs in approximately one-third of individuals treated for longer than 4 weeks.

records.summary: Modafinil is a benzhydryl-class eugeroic stimulant first developed in France in the late 1970s by neurophysiologist Michel Jouvet and Lafon Laboratories. It is the main metabolite of adrafinil[cite:ameline-2020-fsr], with U.S. medical approval granted in 1998[cite:url-dailymed-nlm-nih-gov-druginfo-cfm]. It is prescribed for narcolepsy, sleep apnea, and shift work disorder[cite:url-dailymed-nlm-nih-gov-druginfo-cfm], and is also commonly used off-label as a cognitive enhancer because its stimulant profile is relatively subtle compared with traditional stimulants[citation-needed].
records.title: Modafinil

tolerance.baseline_tolerance: 1-2 weeks
tolerance.full_tolerance: Many modafinil effects may become less pronounced after prolonged repeated use, leading some users to require larger doses for similar results.

routes.bioavailability_notes:
Extensive first-pass metabolism in the liver significantly reduces the amount reaching systemic circulation
Oral doses must be approximately 6 times larger than injected doses to achieve equivalent effects
Absorption occurs in the alkaline environment of the upper intestine

routes.notes: These dose ranges are intended for opioid-naive individuals. Persons with existing opioid tolerance may require different amounts, while those with no tolerance should approach even threshold doses with caution due to the risk of respiratory depression.

routes.half_life_notes: Plasma concentrations typically peak within 30–90 minutes of oral administration. With repeated dosing, steady-state levels are generally achieved after 24–48 hours. The rate of elimination is influenced by factors including sex, age, diet, genetics, and concurrent medications. Morphine may accumulate in adipose tissue, potentially prolonging detection times. Roughly 70–80% of a dose is excreted within 48 hours.

records.summary: Morphine is the principal alkaloid of the opium poppy (Papaver somniferum)[citation-needed] and the prototypical opioid analgesic.[cite:ncbi-mesh-morphine-d009020] First isolated by Friedrich Sertürner in 1805,[cite:pmc-the-isolation-of-morphine-by-serturner] it has served as the foundation from which numerous semi-synthetic opioids have been derived. Morphine produces potent analgesia,[cite:url-ncbi-nlm-nih-gov-books-NBK526115] euphoria,[cite:url-ncbi-nlm-nih-gov-books-NBK526115] and sedation,[cite:url-ncbi-nlm-nih-gov-books-NBK526115] and is used clinically for the management of moderate to severe pain.[cite:url-ncbi-nlm-nih-gov-books-NBK526115] Its use carries significant risks of tolerance, physical dependence,[cite:dailymed-morphine-sulfate-oral-solution] and abuse.[cite:dailymed-morphine-sulfate-oral-solution]
records.title: Morphine

tolerance.baseline_tolerance: After a period of abstinence, tolerance decreases significantly. Users returning to the substance after abstinence should use substantially lower doses than their pre-abstinence amounts, as their previous typical dose may produce life-threatening effects.
tolerance.full_tolerance: Tolerance develops rapidly with repeated use, sometimes after only a short period of consumption. This necessitates progressively higher doses to achieve the same effects.

records.summary: N-Methylbisfluoromodafinil is an obscure nootropic substance of the benzhydryl class. It is the bis-fluoro-N-methyl analogue of modafinil, featuring fluorine substitutions on both of its benzene rings and a methyl group on the amide nitrogen. Despite its structural relationship to modafinil and adrafinil, it has no established research history, and neither pharmacological nor safety-profile similarities to these related compounds should be assumed.

tolerance.full_tolerance: Many effects can become less responsive after sustained repeated use, leading users to need higher amounts for similar results.

records.summary: NEP is a substituted cathinone[cite:godoi-2024-nep-metabolic] that produces stimulating, euphoric, and mildly entactogenic effects. It first appeared on the research chemical market in 2016 as a contemporary designer drug. Structurally related to pentedrone, it differs by an additional ethyl group on the terminal nitrogen, reportedly making it roughly three times as potent.[citation-needed] NEP is also closely related to N-ethylhexedrone and is noted for its relatively short duration of action.[citation-needed]

records.summary: Nicomorphine is a semi-synthetic opioid agonist of the morphine family, classified as both an opioid and a depressant. It is estimated to be two to three times more potent than morphine and is characterized by a notably rapid onset of effects, attributed to its increased lipid solubility. Nicomorphine sees limited medical use in a small number of countries. As with other opioids, it carries significant habit-forming potential.

routes.notes: An average cigarette delivers approximately 2 mg of absorbed nicotine, a reinforcing dose that remains far below toxic levels.

records.summary: Nicotine is a naturally occurring alkaloid found primarily in tobacco and in trace amounts in plants such as tomatoes and aubergines.[citation-needed] It acts as a stimulant at low doses, promoting the release of dopamine, serotonin, and adrenaline,[citation-needed] while higher doses produce calming and muscle-relaxing effects. Widely regarded as one of the most addictive substances known,[cite:statpearls-nicotine-addiction] it is used both recreationally through tobacco products and therapeutically as a smoking cessation aid.[citation-needed]

records.summary: Nitrazepam is a long-acting benzodiazepine hypnotic first synthesized in the late 1950s by Hoffmann-La Roche and introduced medically in 1965 under the brand name Mogadon. It possesses potent sedative, anxiolytic, amnestic, anticonvulsant, and muscle relaxant properties.[citation-needed] Nitrazepam is primarily prescribed for short-term treatment of severe insomnia and disabling anxiety, reducing sleep onset time and increasing sleep duration.[citation-needed] It is also used in managing myoclonic seizures.[cite:mogadon-pm-aapharma-2021][cite:apo-nitrazepam-pm-apotex]

In children treated for epilepsy, tolerance may develop within months of continued use, often necessitating dose escalation.[citation-needed]
